content_voiceover: This question bundles four statements about CML and asks which combination is correct. Statement one is true, cytogenetics combined with FISH or RT-PCR remains standard for confirming the Philadelphia chromosome or BCR-ABL1 fusion in every new CML diagnosis. Statement two is false, asciminib's approval was for adult patients, not as pediatric first-line therapy, so that claim about children is fabricated for the exam. Statement three is false, ASXL1 mutations are generally associated with a worse, not better, response to TKI therapy and portend higher risk disease. Statement four is true, pediatric CML patients treated with front-line imatinib do tend to achieve molecular responses more slowly than adults, yet their overall survival ends up comparable. Combining the two correct statements, one and four, gives answer D.
keypoints: Cytogenetics plus FISH or RT-PCR confirms CML diagnosis in all cases
ASXL1 mutation predicts worse, not better, TKI response
Pediatric CML on imatinib responds more slowly but has similar survival to adults
Watch for fabricated drug approval claims in exam distractors
keypoint_voiceover: Remember, standard CML diagnosis always pairs cytogenetics with FISH or RT-PCR. ASXL1 mutations flag a worse, not favorable, response to TKI therapy. And children with CML on front-line imatinib show slower molecular responses than adults but reach comparable long-term survival, which is why statements one and four are the correct pair here.
